title: Staggered trip windows and tenant-safe containment for dependency failures
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Design and implement staggered trip windows for circuit breakers at the dependency/model/tenant levels to avoid coordinated mass failovers. Tie trip behavior to SLOs and error budgets so that load-shedding and fallback decisions are economically and operationally safe. Ensure safe fallbacks to compatible model variants and regional reroutes, plus an immediate containment mode that limits per-tenant blast radius when downstream dependencies degrade.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant, per-model, and per-dependency breakers exist with configurable thresholds (error-rate, p95 latency, queue-depth)
Breakers support a stanza called 'stagger_window' that probabilistically staggers trip time across regions/instances
SLO-linked policy: when a customer crosses configured error-budget threshold, breaker moves to progressive load-shed policies rather than hard-open where possible
Fallback routing policy automatically selects pre-approved model variants (quantized/cheaper) or regional endpoints with documented degraded quality bounds
Dashboards and alerts created: breaker_state, breaker_trips_by_tenant, fallback_invocations, and impact_on_slo
Canary rollout (10% traffic roll to new logic) with automatic rollback on >2x expected error-rate or customer-visible SLO violations
End-to-end integration tests covering simulated regional latency spikes, dependency blackholes, and noisy neighbor scenarios
Runbook updated with containment steps and safe-unwind choreography for post-incident recovery
implementation_steps: Design breaker schema: thresholds, hysteresis, trip_reason tags, stagger_window params, and fallback_policy references
Extend runtime to honor 'stagger_window' by applying a deterministic jitter based on tenant hash + region seed
Implement SLO adapter: map SLOs/error budgets per tenant to breaker behavior (gradual shedding tiers)
Add fallback selector that evaluates compatibility (tokenizer/seq_len/response-schema) and quality delta before rerouting
Persist breaker state in central metadata store with short TTL and regional caches for low-latency checks
Create observability hooks and emit structured events for every state transition (reason, metrics snapshot, caller context)
Feature-flag rollout and integration tests in staging with synthetic traffic and chaos injection
Gradual production rollout with telemetry gates and on-call notification escalation paths
rollout_plan: Alpha in staging: single region, small tenants only; validate state transitions and metrics
Beta canary: 10% of traffic across two regions for 72h; gating on no SLO regressions and expected breaker behavior
Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks with watch windows and manual hold option
Emergency containment: a tenant isolation toggle to force per-tenant hard-fuse if progressive shedding fails
Post-rollout: 1-week elevated monitoring and follow-up incident retro if any customer-visible impact
testing_plan: Unit tests for breaker state machine and stagger_window jitter function
Integration tests: simulate slow dependency responses and verify fallback selector picks compatible models
Chaos tests: region-level latency injection to ensure stagger prevents simultaneous trips across regions
Load tests: queue-depth based trips under sustained high QPS; validate shedding reduces load to target throughput
Golden-path regression: ensure function/tool calling and structured outputs are unchanged for non-fallback flows
SLO regression harness: baseline run vs new logic using representative prompt sets and traffic fingerprints
